name: AccountButton
description:
The signed-in user account: avatar, display name, optional email and notification count.
Use as a Menu trigger for host-owned profile, preferences and sign-out actions:
`<Menu.Trigger render={<AccountButton … />} />`. Native button props and refs are preserved.
signature: ({ name, email, avatarSrc, unread, className, ...rest }: AccountButtonProps): import("react").JSX.Element

props.name: avatarSrc
props.description: Profile image URL; an initials fallback is used when it is absent.

props.name: email
props.description: Optional second line beneath the name. Omit when the account has no public email address.

props.name: name
props.description: Display name for the signed-in account; also used for its accessible name and avatar fallback.

props.name: unread
props.description: Unread notifications: a count on the avatar's corner (R5.2: the avatar carries them).

props.name: className
props.description: Classes applied to the outer element for layout. Use the component props and theme tokens for its appearance.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The initial value when using the component without controlling its state.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables interaction while retaining the component’s disabled appearance.

props.name: ref
props.description:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).

props.name: value
props.description: The controlled value. Keep it in application state and update it in the change callback.
